---
title: "03 · Can I compare my samples?"
output: html_notebook
---

> **Question:** are the samples comparable, or is one wildly different?
> The plot: the distribution of counts per sample.

## Setup — run this first

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
data_dir <- if (dir.exists("data")) "data" else if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data" else "project/data"
counts <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "gene_counts.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
meta   <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "metadata.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# tidy (one row per gene x sample) + attach the sample info
counts_long <- counts %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(gene_id, gene_name), names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample")
```

## A boxplot per sample

Counts are very skewed, so we plot them on a log scale.

```{r, fig.height=6}
ggplot(counts_long, aes(x = sample, y = log10(count + 1), fill = lifestyle)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log10(count + 1)")
```
